terminal_record.title: Trump Administration Asked Senior Security Job Candidates Questions About January 6
terminal_record.description_short: The Washington Post reported yes-or-no political questions for top intelligence and law-enforcement candidates, including whether January 6 was “an inside job.”
terminal_record.description_medium: On February 8, 2025, The Washington Post reported that candidates for top intelligence and law-enforcement positions in the Trump administration were asked yes-or-no questions about the 2020 election and January 6, including whether January 6 was “an inside job.” The report said the questions appeared designed to test candidates’ acceptance of the president’s claims. It does not describe signed oaths imposed on career employees.
terminal_record.description_long: The Washington Post reported that candidates for top intelligence and law-enforcement jobs in the Trump administration faced yes-or-no questions about the 2020 election and its aftermath. One example was whether January 6 was “an inside job.” The article said the questions appeared designed to determine whether candidates had embraced President Trump’s false claims about the election, citing people familiar with screening cases. The report concerns candidates for senior national-security posts, not a government-wide requirement that career employees sign personal loyalty statements. The supplied frozen card asserted such oaths, refusals, and administrative leave, but the accessed reporting does not establish those claims. This repaired entry is limited to the interview-screening questions described by the Post. It does not claim that every nominee received the questions, that the questions were written or ordered personally by Trump, that a candidate was rejected for an answer, or that employees were required to swear loyalty to him. The article path dates the report to February 8, and its extracted page states it was updated February 9, 2025.
